# Casting a managed voice

## Which voice already applies

Read `voyager voice agent production` before searching. Each speaker's entry in `resolutions`
is one of:

| `kind`  | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                          | What to do                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `voice` | A structured choice applies. `source` says where it came from: `explicit`, `production`, `project`, `workspace` or `user`. `verified: false` means it was not re-checked online. | Use it. Do not audition or re-cast unless the user asks.                                                                                                                     |
| `stale` | The choice was saved under another Voyager workspace (`other_workspace`) or the voice was withdrawn (`revoked`).                                                                 | Tell the user plainly ("the saved narrator isn't in this workspace") and ask for a replacement, or recast with auditions if they delegated it. Existing takes stay playable. |
| `prose` | Only prose guidance exists (the `creativeVoice` preference).                                                                                                                     | Treat it as the casting brief for the search; it never names a voice by itself.                                                                                              |

A stale level never falls through to a lower one, so a stale production cast is
not silently replaced by the project default.

## What the catalog contains

- Voyager voice ids look like `vox_…`. Never ask for, pass or show a provider's
  voice id, except a clone the user made on their own provider key
  ([cloning](#cloning-a-real-voice)).
- Each voice lists `languages`, `labels` (accent, age, gender, use case,
  descriptive words), `compatibleModels`, `recommendedModels` and an
  `availability`. A voice whose availability is not available cannot be cast.
- Voice names such as "Jessica" or "Brian" are catalog display names. Names used
  by the separate speech shortcuts (`voyager models voices`) are a different list;
  never mix the two.

## Search well

`voyager voice agent search` takes `query`, `language`, `accent`, `useCase`, `gender`,
`cursor` and `limit` (1–30, default 10), or `voiceId` for one voice.

## Fish Audio voices

Some workspaces also list Fish Audio voices. Each search result names its
`engine`: `elevenlabs` or `fishaudio`.

- When the user names a Fish Audio voice or creator ("use Uncle Roger"), search
  with that name as `query`, `provider: fishaudio` and `category: featured`. Featured
  voices are licensed by Fish Audio and list their `creator`. If nothing matches,
  repeat the search without `category`.
- If the preference block says `Voice engine: … Fish Audio`, search with
  `provider: fishaudio` first. Otherwise search the way you already do.
- Cast a Fish Audio voice like any other: `cast: {voice}`. Its takes render on
  Fish Audio, and Voyager picks the model, so do not set `modelId`. In one
  production, speakers can use voices from different engines.
- For an acted scene, use Fish Audio Drama 3 (`fishaudio-native-drama-3`). It
  reads plain-language `[directions]` before the words they apply to. A ranged
  direction named `whisper`, `emphasis`, `soft`, `fast`, `slow`, `stress` or
  `forceful` changes only those words.
- For a dialogue take, read the [speaker range eligibility rule](../SKILL.md#generating-a-take).
- Fish Audio voices cannot convert a recording, and they cannot make music or
  sound effects. Use ElevenLabs for those.

Catalog samples play in the Voice panel; tool results never carry preview
links.

## Auditions

- **Cost.** Each
  candidate costs a short generation, so state the combined estimate
  (`totalEstimatedCredits`) as a receipt after submission. Before the paid call,
  follow [managed narration preflight](../SKILL.md#managed-narration-preflight)
  for the credit quote and task-go-ahead exception before auditioning.
- **Direction.** Candidates use the production's model, preset and rules, so
  save pronunciation rules before auditioning a hard name.
- **Waiting.** `voyager voice agent audition` returns at once, and its jobs never resume the
  conversation. Get each candidate's `jobId` from `voyager voice agent take {attemptId}`, wait
  on them together with `voyager jobs wait JOB_ID... --json`, then read
  `voyager voice agent take {auditionId}`; never end the turn on pending candidates.
- **Reuse.** An identical earlier successful audition is reused without another
  charge.

### Presenting the choice

End each option's description with the take's
`audioAbsolutePath` in angle brackets:

```text
Reassuring and unhurried </Users/k/Projects/Honeydew/voice/vprod_…/vtake_….mp3>
```

Use the
absolute path from `voyager voice agent take` or `voyager voice agent production`, never the relative
`audioPath`; only absolute paths become play buttons. The app hides the path and
plays each sample beside its option; playing never answers the question. Never ask
about a voice without its take or preview.

Alternatively call `voyager voice agent open` with `view: "voice"`: it plays the candidates loudness-matched and
has a "Use voice" button.

A voice pick does not approve the script.

## Recording the choice

- After the answer, call `voyager voice agent production_update` with `cast: {voice}` (and
  `speakerId` for a second speaker). Only this sets the voice; an answered question or
  a played sample does not.
- `cast.alsoProjectDefault: true` also makes it the project's default voice. Do
  it when the user says so ("use her for everything in this project").
- The user default is set in Settings → Creative preferences → Default voice;
  agents cannot write it. `preferences_save` saves prose casting guidance only.

## Voices like this clip

When the user gives a recording and wants voices like it ("find me voices like
this", "sounds like my recording"), match the clip instead of searching text:

1. **Match.** `voyager voice agent similar` with `recordingPath` (the clip as
   attached, or in the conversation's folder; extract a video's audio first) and
   optionally `limit` (1–10, default 5). It is free, keeps nothing of the clip, and
   answers library `vox_` voices, most similar first; Voyager Free is refused (custom voices need Starter). With none, search
   the catalog by description.
2. **Their own voice?** Only if the user said the clip is their own voice (never
   infer it) and `capabilities` `narration.plan` is `ultra`, `gigamax` or `null`,
   also offer it conditionally: "If your Voice tab shows Your voice, you can clone
   it there." You cannot detect whether managed cloning is available, so never
   promise it. Only the user can start that clone, and only of
   their own voice ([consent](#cloning-a-real-voice)).

Library voices render on ElevenLabs models only; never pair one with a Fish Audio
model. One its owner withdraws turns stale like any other
([which voice already applies](#which-voice-already-applies)).

## Cloning a real voice

Use this when the user wants a real person's voice: their own, or a speaker whose
recorded reads came out flat and should be redone with more expression.

There are two cloning paths. Offer only the one the user can use:

- **Own key** (you run it): when `voyager connections list --json` lists
  `elevenlabs` as connected (or `inworld`/`fishaudio` with `--provider`). It can clone the user
  or another consenting speaker, into the user's own provider account, never on
  Voyager credits. Follow the steps below.
- **Clone my voice** (the user runs it): Voyager's managed cloning of the user's own
  voice, on Ultra and GigaMax™ plans for 50 credits a clone (re-recording costs the
  same). You cannot run it or check whether this account has it: the
  `voice.clone*` commands are refused to agents (`UI_REQUIRED`). Mention it only
  conditionally: "If your Voice tab shows **Your voice**, choose **Clone my
  voice** there to clone your own voice." Never promise it is there. Once made, the user casts it with **Use** under Your voice, and it
  narrates as the production's cast voice (always on Eleven v3). It never clones
  someone else's voice; for that, only the own-key path applies.
- **Neither** (no connected key, and the user cannot or would rather not use
  Clone my voice): say cloning needs their own ElevenLabs key in Connectors →
  Providers, and offer casting a similar voice or converting a recorded
  performance ([performance](performance.md)).

Own-key cloning:

1. **Consent first.** Ask, unless the user already said so: is it their own voice,
   or do they have that person's permission to clone it? Without a yes, do not
   clone; offer [a similar voice](#voices-like-this-clip) or converting a recorded performance
   ([performance](performance.md)). Never clone a public figure or anyone else who
   has not agreed.
2. **Their own ElevenLabs key.** Cloning runs only on the ElevenLabs key in
   Connectors → Providers (check `voyager connections list --json`; the
   capabilities' `narration.ownElevenLabsKey` is set only when managed narration is
   blocked), never on Voyager credits, and the clone lands in the user's ElevenLabs
   voice library. Without the key, do not run `speech clone`; offer the paths above.
3. **Clone.** Pass one or more clean recordings of that one speaker (a minute or
   more in total, no music or other voices; extract a video's audio first):
   `voyager speech clone take-1.wav take-2.wav --name "Ana" --remove-background-noise`.
   Add `--description` noting the consent ("Ana's own voice, cloned with her
   permission"). It answers the new `voiceId`.
4. **Narrate.** `voyager speech narrate --voice VOICE_ID --text "..."` runs on the
   same key with Eleven v4, so audio tags such as `[excited]` or `[whispers]`
   direct the delivery. No managed takes, rules or repairs on this route. To redo a
   recorded read in the clone, `voyager speech convert READ.wav --voice VOICE_ID`.

If ElevenLabs refuses because the plan has no voice cloning, or the voice library
is full, tell the user exactly that from the error (they upgrade or free a slot
in ElevenLabs) and offer casting meanwhile. Do not retry on another route.

**On Inworld instead.** When the user wants the clone on their Inworld key, add
`--provider inworld`: `voyager speech clone take.wav --name "Ana" --provider inworld`.
Inworld clones from one clear WAV or MP3 of 10 to 30 seconds (it ignores anything past
30), and the key needs Voice write access. Narrate the answered `voiceId` with
`voyager speech narrate --model inworld-tts-2 --voice VOICE_ID --text "..."`. Consent
first, exactly as above.

# Performance conversion

## The recording

- **The user records it.** You cannot record. Open the Voice panel's recorder
  with `voyager voice agent open {view: "record"}` (it opens the Takes tab with the recorder
  sheet) and ask the user to record there, or ask for
  a file (any common audio format; video soundtracks work too).
- **Length:** 1 second to 5 minutes after trimming, up to 50 MiB. Longer reads
  are split into sections at natural pauses and converted separately.

## Models

| Model                                             | Use                     |
| ------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------- |
| `elevenlabs-native-sts-multilingual-v2` (default) | Any supported language. |
| `elevenlabs-native-sts-english-v2`                | English only.           |

Only these two models convert. Their
controls are `stability`, `similarity_boost`, `style`, `use_speaker_boost`,
`remove_background_noise` and `seed`; presets apply as for text models. Tags and
pronunciation rules do not apply: the performance decides.

## On the user's own ElevenLabs key

With an ElevenLabs key in Connectors → Providers (`narration.ownElevenLabsKey`),
`voyager speech convert READ.wav --voice VOICE` converts on that key instead of
Voyager credits: `VOICE` is a premade name (`George`) or a voice ID from the
user's ElevenLabs library, such as their clone. `--model` is
`elevenlabs-sts-multilingual-v2` (default) or `elevenlabs-sts-english-v2`;
`--parameters` takes the controls above. Managed `vox_` voices, takes and the
Voice panel are not on this route; it returns a media job. Use it without a plan
or when Voyager credits run out.

## Converting

1. **Cost and approval.** Conversion is billed per second of the trimmed recording,
   not per character. Before the paid call, read
   [managed narration preflight](../SKILL.md#managed-narration-preflight)
   for unknown-cost authorization; a narration text quote does not price this recording.
2. **Convert** with `voyager voice agent convert`: `productionId`, `expectedRevision`,
   `requestKey`, `recordingPath`, and optionally `voice`, `modelId`,
   `settings`, `trimStartUs`/`trimEndUs`, `range` and `maxEstimatedCredits`.
   - `recordingPath` is the file attached in this chat (its saved path), or a
     path in the conversation's folder. Voyager copies it into
     `voice/<productionId>/recordings/`.
   - `voice` defaults to the production's cast.
   - `range` ties the converted take to the script words it performs.
3. **Wait** exactly as for a text take ([takes and repairs](../SKILL.md#takes-approval-and-repairs)).

## After conversion

- **No word timings.** Conversion returns no alignment (`alignment: "none"`),
  so captions, assembly and exact pauses are unavailable for that take until it
  is transcribed (`voyager speech transcribe TAKE --local --output .voyager/tmp/TAKE-transcript`).
- A converted take can be approved like a full take.

# Standalone narration routes

When the user explicitly asks for Gemini TTS or their own Google key, use
`gemini-3.8-flash-tts` (alias `google/gemini-3.8-flash-tts`) through `voyager models`
or `voyager speech narrate --model gemini-3.8-flash-tts --voice Kore`. A Google key
in Connectors → Providers runs it on any Voyager plan, billed to that key with no
Voyager credits. When they ask for their Google key, estimate and submit through
`models` with `pin: "google"`. Otherwise estimate first and relay the payer; if
the estimate returns `credits.pin: "google"`, submit through `models` with that pin. The prompt is verbatim speech;
`style_instructions` directs delivery separately. For dialogue, omit prompt and
use native input with two `speakers` (`speaker_id`, `voice`) and ordered `turns`
(`speaker_id`, `text`, optional `style_instructions`). `models show` and
`models voices` list its schema and voices. These jobs return WAV files outside
managed voice productions; wait for the media job before using the result.

When the user asks for Inworld, or a connected Inworld key (`voyager connections list --json`)
is their only narration route, use `voyager speech narrate --model inworld-tts-2 --voice
Ashley --text "..."` (`inworld-tts-2-flash` for cheap drafts). Read `voyager models show inworld-tts-2 --json` and estimate for billing and input limits. This standalone route has no managed takes, rules or repairs. `voyager models voices inworld-tts-2` lists the key's voices,
including its clones. A bracketed instruction before the words, such as `[say warmly]`, steers
TTS-2. Wait for its media job before using the result.

## Standalone speech models

| Need | Candidates and live sources | Selection-relevant distinction |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A one-off spoken line outside a voice production | Voyager's audio models (`GET /v1/media/models`): the `eleven-v4`, `eleven-v4-turbo` and `eleven-v3` shortcuts, and `speech narrate` | Read `voyager models show elevenlabs-eleven-v4 --json` (or `elevenlabs-eleven-v4-turbo` / `elevenlabs-eleven-v3`) for character limits, voice defaults and native settings. Turbo suits drafts. `voyager models voices eleven-v4` lists premade voices. The fal-hosted copies run only when named: `elevenlabs-eleven-v4-fal` and the rest (unlisted), or a fal endpoint such as `elevenlabs/tts/eleven-v4`; fal's `text-to-dialogue/eleven-v3` stays fal-only. The fal Turbo v2.5 endpoint is retired. No productions, pronunciation rules or takes on this route. |
| Explicit pauses, pronunciation and voice controls on fal, when chosen explicitly | [MiniMax Speech 2.8 HD](https://fal.ai/models/fal-ai/minimax/speech-2.8-hd/llms.txt), [Turbo](https://fal.ai/models/fal-ai/minimax/speech-2.8-turbo/llms.txt) | `fal-ai/minimax/speech-2.8-hd` or `fal-ai/minimax/speech-2.8-turbo`. |

## Speech with pause markup: MiniMax Speech 2.8 HD and Turbo

- Pauses: `<#1.5#>` between spoken words. `voyager models show fal-ai/minimax/speech-2.8-hd --json` (or Turbo) lists pause ranges and placement constraints.
- Interjections in parentheses: `(laughs)`, `(sighs)`, `(breath)`, `(gasps)`, `(sniffs)`, `(coughs)`, `(groans)`
  and more in MiniMax's list. Fal spells `(clears throat)`, MiniMax `(clear-throat)`: test before relying on it.
- Use `voice_setting` for delivery and `language_boost` for language; read the model card for controls and output defaults. Set `output_format: "url"` when you need an audio URL.

When the estimate’s `payerNote` names a shortcut for the user’s own key, run that shortcut rather than a named hosted copy; `pin: "moda"` keeps a deliberately chosen hosted copy on Voyager credits. Use the own-key fallback only when the managed voice workflow explicitly authorizes it; never silently substitute a standalone model for an unavailable managed take.

For ElevenLabs delivery tags, see [voice direction](../SKILL.md#voices-elevenlabs-v4-v4-turbo-and-v3).

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Diff a finished voice take's transcript against its script, line by line.

usage: check-take.py SCRIPT TAKE --transcript FILE

SCRIPT is a JSON array with one entry per line: a string, or {"text": "...", "asr": "..."}
where "asr" is what the transcriber writes for a name or figure the script spells differently.
TAKE is the take's audio; FILE is DIR/transcript.json from
`voyager speech transcribe TAKE --local --output DIR`.

Words compare lowercase without punctuation. Numbers 0-999 equal their spoken words ("40" is
"forty", "hundred and five" is "hundred five"); $1,000 is 1000; 3.5, 1:30, 24/7 and 40% keep
their . : / %, so put their spoken form in "asr" when the transcriber writes words. Prints
JSON: {"ok", "lines": [{"index", "text", "ok", "heard"}], "heard"}. Exit 0 when every line
matches, 1 when some differ, 2 when the check could not run.
"""
import argparse
import difflib
import json
import re
import sys

ONES = "zero one two three four five six seven eight nine ten eleven twelve thirteen fourteen fifteen sixteen seventeen eighteen nineteen".split()
TENS = "x x twenty thirty forty fifty sixty seventy eighty ninety".split()


def number_words(value):
    words = []
    if value >= 100:
        words += [ONES[value // 100], "hundred"]
        value %= 100
    if value >= 20:
        words.append(TENS[value // 10])
        value %= 10
    if value or not words:
        words.append(ONES[value])
    return words


def normalize(text):
    """The words to compare: lowercase, no punctuation, plain integers below 1000 spelled out.

    Decimals, times, fractions and percents keep their . : / % so 1.7 never reads as 17.
    """
    words = []
    for raw in text.lower().replace("'", "").replace("-", " ").split():
        word = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]", "", raw)
        if not word:
            continue
        kept = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9.:/%]", "", raw).strip(".:/")
        if re.search(r"\d[.:/]\d|\d%", kept):
            words.append(kept)
        elif re.fullmatch(r"0|[1-9]\d{0,2}", word):
            words += number_words(int(word))
        elif word == "and" and words and words[-1] == "hundred":
            continue
        else:
            words.append(word)
    return words


def fail(message):
    """Exit 2, the documented code for a check that could not run, with one line and no traceback."""
    sys.stderr.write(f"check-take.py: {message}\n")
    sys.exit(2)


def compare(lines, transcript):
    want, owner = [], []
    for index, line in enumerate(lines):
        entry = line if isinstance(line, dict) else {"text": line}
        words = normalize(entry.get("asr") or entry["text"])
        want += words
        owner += [index] * len(words)
    heard = normalize(" ".join(word["text"] for word in transcript.get("words", [])))
    got = [[] for _ in lines]
    wrong = set()
    for tag, a0, a1, b0, b1 in difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, want, heard, autojunk=False).get_opcodes():
        if tag == "equal":
            for offset in range(a1 - a0):
                got[owner[a0 + offset]].append(heard[b0 + offset])
            continue
        # Extra words at a boundary belong to the line that follows them, or the last line.
        lines_hit = sorted({owner[i] for i in range(a0, a1)}) or [owner[a0] if a0 < len(owner) else len(lines) - 1]
        wrong.update(lines_hit)
        got[lines_hit[0]] += heard[b0:b1]
    report = [
        {
            "index": index,
            "text": (line if isinstance(line, dict) else {"text": line})["text"],
            "ok": index not in wrong,
            "heard": " ".join(got[index]),
        }
        for index, line in enumerate(lines)
    ]
    return {"ok": not wrong, "lines": report, "heard": " ".join(heard)}


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    parser.add_argument("script")
    parser.add_argument("take")
    parser.add_argument("--transcript", required=True, help="the take's transcript.json")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    with open(args.script, encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        lines = json.load(handle)
    if not isinstance(lines, list) or not lines:
        fail("SCRIPT must be a non-empty JSON array of lines")
    with open(args.transcript, encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        transcript = json.load(handle)
    result = compare(lines, transcript)
    print(json.dumps(result, ensure_ascii=False, indent=1))
    sys.exit(0 if result["ok"] else 1)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

import importlib.util
import json
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest

spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("check_take", Path(__file__).with_name("check-take.py"))
check_take = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
spec.loader.exec_module(check_take)


class CheckTakeTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def run_check(self, lines, heard):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="voyager-take-") as folder:
            root = Path(folder)
            (root / "script.json").write_text(json.dumps(lines), encoding="utf-8")
            words = [{"id": f"w{index:04d}", "text": word, "start": {"timescale": 1, "value": "0"}, "end": {"timescale": 1, "value": "0"}, "conf": 1} for index, word in enumerate(heard.split())]
            (root / "transcript.json").write_text(json.dumps({"schema": "video-transcript/1", "language": "en", "words": words, "segments": []}), encoding="utf-8")
            result = subprocess.run(["python3", str(Path(__file__).with_name("check-take.py")), str(root / "script.json"), str(root / "take.wav"), "--transcript", str(root / "transcript.json")], capture_output=True, text=True)
            return result.returncode, json.loads(result.stdout)

    def test_numbers_punctuation_and_case_match(self):
        code, result = self.run_check(["Save 40 dollars today.", "That's one hundred and five reasons, Voyager!"], "Save forty dollars today. thats 105 reasons voyager")
        self.assertEqual(code, 0)
        self.assertTrue(result["ok"])
        self.assertEqual([line["ok"] for line in result["lines"]], [True, True])
        self.assertEqual(result["lines"][1]["heard"], "thats one hundred five reasons voyager")

    def test_a_misread_line_is_named_with_what_was_heard(self):
        code, result = self.run_check(["Welcome to Voyager.", "Render in forty seconds.", "Then share it."], "Welcome to Voyager. Render in fourteen seconds. Then share it.")
        self.assertEqual(code, 1)
        self.assertEqual([line["ok"] for line in result["lines"]], [True, False, True])
        self.assertEqual(result["lines"][1]["heard"], "render in fourteen seconds")

    def test_asr_overrides_a_line_and_formatted_numbers_stay_as_written(self):
        lines = [{"text": "Moda renders at 3.5x speed.", "asr": "Moda renders at three point five x speed."}, "Ask for Jhh3."]
        code, result = self.run_check(lines, "Moda renders at three point five x speed. Ask for J H H three.")
        self.assertEqual(code, 1)
        self.assertEqual([line["ok"] for line in result["lines"]], [True, False])
        lines[1] = {"text": "Ask for Jhh3.", "asr": "Ask for J H H three."}
        code, result = self.run_check(lines, "Moda renders at three point five x speed. Ask for J H H three.")
        self.assertEqual(code, 0)
        self.assertEqual(result["lines"][1]["text"], "Ask for Jhh3.")

    def test_a_decimal_keeps_its_point(self):
        code, result = self.run_check(["Version 1.7 ships today."], "Version 1.7 ships today.")
        self.assertEqual(code, 0)
        self.assertEqual(result["lines"][0]["heard"], "version 1.7 ships today")
        code, result = self.run_check(["It costs 1.70 now."], "It costs 17.0 now.")
        self.assertEqual(code, 1)
        self.assertEqual(result["lines"][0]["heard"], "it costs 17.0 now")
        self.assertEqual(check_take.normalize("It took 1:30, cost $1,000 and **1.7x** or +40%."), ["it", "took", "1:30", "cost", "1000", "and", "1.7x", "or", "40%"])
        self.assertEqual(check_take.normalize("Ten 1,000. 1000"), ["ten", "1000", "1000"])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

---
name: voiceover
description: "Generate narration with Voyager voices, revise managed voice takes, or clean and repair speech recordings."
applications:
  - id: moda
    role: primary
  - id: ffmpeg
    role: alternative
voyager:
  schemaVersion: 1
  design: none
---

Finish audio with the bundled FFmpeg unless the user chose another tool.

## Stock narration

Voyager Free reports `free_stock_only`: premade narration on Eleven v4 Turbo, 3 generations a month, at most 4,000 characters each, with no managed takes or rules. Narrate the whole script in one generation where it fits, since every take and retake counts. Past the month's 3, Voyager refuses with `free_media_limit` (`media=voice`) until the month renews: tell the user and ask how to finish (their own ElevenLabs key, a captions-led cut, or upgrading); never retry or switch voice models. Run `voyager voice agent narrate_stock`, then wait with `voyager jobs wait JOB_ID --json`. Its outputs include `transcript.json` with provider word timings when available: use it for captions and speech edits instead of transcribing narration you just generated. If the job returns only audio, timings are unavailable; never assume cloud transcription is included on Free.

On Windows/PowerShell, write operation arguments to a UTF-8 JSON file and run
`voyager voice agent narrate_stock --input '@narration.json' --json` (or use the
structured MCP voice tool). Use `--input -` for piped JSON. Avoid inline JSON in
native CLI arguments: PowerShell can strip its quotes. The inline examples below
work on macOS/Linux; on Windows pass the same object through a file instead.

For Gemini TTS on a connected provider key, see [own-key narration routes](references/standalone-narration.md). When the user asks for Inworld, or a connected Inworld key is their only narration route, check `voyager connections list --json` and use `voyager speech narrate --model inworld-tts-2` per that reference. These routes return media jobs outside managed voice productions.

## Finish a recording

Cleaning, repairing, levelling, joining or comping takes, mixing and delivering an existing recording: one FFmpeg filter chain or script.

- To fix words in a person's recording, use `voyager transcript replace` ([edit by text](../edit-video/SKILL.md#edit-by-text)); it uses their saved clone, or a copy of their voice once they consent in the card. To change generated narration, regenerate the line instead.
- Word-level joins, comps and cuts go through [speech edits](../edit-video/SKILL.md#speech-edits).
- For a person's quiet recording, denoise before adding gain, cap the gain to avoid raising the noise floor, and preserve natural dynamics rather than forcing a loudness target. Review the processed voice stem, not the mix, with `voyager media review PROCESSED --audio-source ORIGINAL` so a raised noise floor or crushed dynamics are flagged.
- Music bed: [make-music](../make-music/SKILL.md). Mix and delivery loudness: [make-sound](../make-sound/SKILL.md#mix-to-the-destination).

### Transcription and isolation models

| Need | Candidates and live sources | Selection-relevant distinction |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Transcript with word timing and speakers | [Scribe v2](https://fal.ai/models/fal-ai/elevenlabs/speech-to-text/scribe-v2/llms.txt) | `fal-ai/elevenlabs/speech-to-text/scribe-v2`: word timings, language detection, diarization, event tags and keyterms. |
| Dialogue cleanup or a particular sound stem | [Eleven isolation](https://fal.ai/models/fal-ai/elevenlabs/audio-isolation/llms.txt), [SAM Audio](https://fal.ai/models/fal-ai/sam-audio/separate/llms.txt), [span separation](https://fal.ai/models/fal-ai/sam-audio/span-separate/llms.txt) | Voice isolation versus text/span-directed extraction into target and residual. |

## Generate narration with managed voice tools

Managed voices are the default for narration and replacement lines; Eleven v4, v4 Turbo and v3 have their delivery guidance below. Use Gemini TTS or Inworld when requested, following the standalone narration routes; follow the managed workflow’s explicit own-key fallback when managed voice is unavailable.

For a model the user names or an unusual job, `voyager models list --query "speech" --json` covers the long tail. `voyager models show MODEL --json` answers inputs and limits, `voyager models estimate` answers price, speed and payer, and `voyager models docs MODEL --json` supplies vendor documentation for fal endpoints. Managed models and voices instead come from `voyager voice agent capabilities` and `voyager voice agent search`, never `models list` or `models voices`.

Use `voyager voice agent OPERATION --input '{…}' --json` in a conversation; `open` shows the Voice panel. `--input '@file.json'` (or `--input -` for stdin) reads JSON without shell quoting; `--input-file PATH` remains supported. `voyager voice agent describe --input '{"operation":"production_update"}'` returns the operation’s exact fields and revision preconditions. Identity comes from the live session token; never supply a thread or project id. Call `voyager voice agent capabilities` once per task, before writing a narrated script; if unavailable, say why and stop managed voice work. `narration.status` `signed_out` or `paid_plan_required` blocks only these managed tools: a connected ElevenLabs key (`narration.ownElevenLabsKey`) still runs `voyager speech narrate` (Eleven v4 by default; premade or the user's ElevenLabs library voices; no takes, rules or repairs): narrate on it without asking unless the user wants a managed Voyager voice, and say those limits in one line. Without that key, check `voyager connections list --json` for the Inworld fallback above before going captions-led. With neither key, build a captions-led cut (on-screen text carries the script) without stopping, mention once that narration needs a paid plan or the user's own ElevenLabs key, and offer to add it later; a `PLAN_REQUIRED` take means the same. On a billing error never switch voice models or speech routes, except to that own-key route when there is no plan or no Voyager credits left.

`voyager voice agent production`'s `resolutions` decide the voice: explicit choice, production cast, then project, workspace, user defaults. Report a stale voice (other workspace, withdrawn); the user or a delegated recast replaces it, never silently. "Voice: for voiceover and narration, use …" is casting guidance, not a voice. Voice cloning has two paths ([cloning](references/casting.md#cloning-a-real-voice)); offer only one the user can use. You run `voyager speech clone` only when `voyager connections list --json` lists the user's own ElevenLabs key (or Inworld with `--provider inworld`), never on Voyager credits, and their ElevenLabs plan must include it; confirm consent first. Managed "Clone my voice" is the user's own action in the Voice panel, on Ultra and GigaMax™ plans and still rolling out: you cannot create a clone, so only when `narration.plan` is `ultra`, `gigamax` or `null` say that if their Voice tab shows Your voice, they can clone their own voice there. Without a key, offer that, casting or conversion ([performance](references/performance.md)).

Search includes your saved cloned voices first by name; `voyager voice agent search "Name"` finds one, and `--category mine` (alias `cloned`) lists only yours. Cast the returned `voiceId` directly with `production_update cast.voice`; a saved clone uses Eleven v3.

A named Fish Audio voice (for example Uncle Roger) is a search with `provider: fishaudio`. See [casting](references/casting.md#fish-audio-voices). A recording to match ("voices like this", "options from this audio", "sounds like my recording") goes to `voyager voice agent similar`, never to text search: see [voices like this clip](references/casting.md#voices-like-this-clip).

A message like "Narrate with Inworld voice NAME (ID, MODEL)", from the Voice panel's Use in chat, is an explicit choice: narrate with that ID and model without asking.

### Casting and delivery

Skip auditions when the voice is resolved, named, "You decide" or the user said go ahead, even when no voice default is saved.

Save script changes with `production_update`; the chat and question card preview the saved script. On own-key routes there is no production, so include the script in the reply when presenting it for review. Voice selection and script approval are separate; honor explicit requests to review either. See [casting](references/casting.md) for auditions and saving a cast.

Report any requested presets, tags or controls the model cannot apply.

## Directing the performance

`voyager voice agent capabilities` is the authority for what each model accepts.

### Read the manifest first

`voyager voice agent capabilities` returns, per model: `operation` (text to speech or speech
to speech), `maxCharacters` or `maxSeconds`, the number of `languages`,
`controls` (name, type, allowed values or range, default), `presets`, `tags`,
`pronunciation` (`inline`, `dictionary` or `none`), `contextStitching`,
`repairPassage` and `alignment`, plus plain-language `notes`. Pass
`refresh: true` only when the user signed in to Voyager again or the result looks stale.

`status: "unavailable"` means paid voice work is unavailable.

Eleven Turbo v2.5 is retired. A production or call that still names
`elevenlabs-native-turbo-v2.5` runs on v4 Turbo, and the Voice panel says so.

- Changing the production's model is `voyager voice agent production_update {modelId}`.
  Existing takes keep their model.

### Presets

Every text model offers three presets, applied before explicit settings:

| Preset | UI label | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `natural` | Natural | The default. A person explaining something to a friend. |
| `expressive` | More expressive | Varied, emotive reads, ads and characters. |
| `steady` | Steady | Instructions, legal copy, long even reads. Can drift toward monotone. |

Set the preset with `voyager voice agent production_update {delivery: {preset}}`.

### Explicit controls

Put overrides in `delivery.settings`, using only names the model lists. Observed
controls:

| Control | v4 / v4 Turbo | v3 | Multilingual v2 | Flash v2.5 | Speech to speech |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `stability` | 0–1 | enum `creative`, `natural`, `robust` | 0–1 | 0–1 | 0–1 |
| `similarity_boost` | 0–1 | – | 0–1 | 0–1 | 0–1 |
| `style` | – | – | 0–1 | – | 0–1 |
| `use_speaker_boost` | – | – | yes | – | yes |
| `speed` | – | – | 0.7–1.2 | 0.7–1.2 | – |
| `language_code` | yes | yes | – | yes | – |
| `apply_text_normalization` | `auto`, `on`, `off` | `auto`, `on`, `off` | `auto`, `on`, `off` | `auto`, `off` | – |
| `seed` | integer | integer | integer | integer | integer |
| `remove_background_noise` | – | – | – | – | yes |

### Audio tags (v4, v4 Turbo and v3)

Tags are square-bracketed words the model performs rather than reads, such as
`[warmly]`, `[excited]`, `[whispers]`, `[laughs]`, `[short pause]`.

On v4 and v4 Turbo a tag can be a short plain-language direction, and several
can share one bracket: `[lower, thoughtful]`, `[quietly curious]`. Each model's `tags`
entry gives the allowed pattern (v4 allows capitals and commas, up to 60
characters) and a vocabulary of tested words.

- A global tag (`delivery.tag`, for example `warmly`) sets the opening tone.
- A direction annotation tags one span: `voyager voice agent production_update {annotations:
  [{kind: "direction", locator: {text: "introducing Voyager"}, tag: "excited",
  instruction: "lift on the reveal"}]}`. See [annotation updates](#edit-a-script-in-place-from-chat) for how to preserve existing notes.

### Pauses

- **Pause annotations** (`kind: "pause"`, `pauseMs` 50–10000, at a word
  boundary) mark where an exact pause belongs. They are never sent to the model
  (the compile result lists them as `pause_is_edit`); after the take exists,
  apply each one as an exact pause edit.
- **An exact pause** of a given length is a local audio edit on an aligned take
  (`voyager voice agent repair {kind: "pause"}`), with no charge. See
  [takes and repairs](#takes-approval-and-repairs).
- On v3 the `[short pause]` or `[long pause]` tags ask for longer pauses.

- The character limit counts the compiled text the model receives (tags and
  inline pronunciation included), so a script near the limit can exceed it after
  compilation.

The delivery brief and annotation
instructions are never read aloud or sent to the model.

## Voices: ElevenLabs v4, v4 Turbo and v3

These are the model's own rules, on top of the direction above.

- A tag carries forward until the next one; add a tag where the delivery shifts, one per clause.
  Put nuance in one bracket: `[whispering, playful]`.
- Write tags as voice qualities. v4 also makes sound effects, so `[applause]` or `[gunshot]` is a
  sound, and a noun-like tag can be heard as one: prefer `[low, gravelly voice]`.
- Ellipses add a pause and weight; capitals add emphasis. No SSML: `<break>` does nothing on v4 or v3.
- Tags work best when the voice already has that delivery; a calm narrator will not shout well.
- Emotion written as narration ("she said sadly") is spoken aloud. Use a tag instead.
- v4 reads another language fluently without the voice's native accent; `[strong X accent]` is experimental.

## Pronunciation

### The rule

| Field | Rules |
| --- | --- |
| `phrase` | The written word or phrase, 1–100 characters, whole words only. No `[ ] / < > { }`, tabs or line breaks. |
| `respelling` | Required. A plain sound-alike most people can read: `MOH-duh`, `kwin-OH-uh`. Stress in capitals, syllables with hyphens. |
| `ipa` | Optional, without slashes: `ˈmoʊdə`. Only IPA letters and marks; uppercase ASCII, digits, X-SAMPA or ARPAbet are refused. |
| `locale` | Defaults to the production language's primary subtag (`en`). `null` means every language. |
| `matching` | `case_insensitive` (default) or `case_sensitive` (for "US" the country versus "us"). |

Write a respelling first; it works on every text model, and it is what Eleven
v4 and v4 Turbo use. Add IPA when the respelling is ambiguous and you know the
IPA; Eleven v3 uses it, other models ignore it and use the respelling.

### Scope

| Scope | Applies to | Stored | Use for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `production` | This production only | In the project | A one-off: a character name, an unusual read for this script. |
| `project` | Every production in the project | In the project | The client's brand and product names. |
| `workspace` | Every project of the connected Voyager workspace | Workspace pronunciation dictionary, append-only revisions | Names the whole team uses. Ask before writing here; teammates share it. |

Save with `voyager voice agent lexicon {action: "save", scope, productionId, rule}`. To change
a rule, save again with its `ruleId` and `expectedRevision` (local scopes) or
with `dictionaryId` and the dictionary's current revision as `expectedRevision`
(workspace). `action: "retire"` removes a rule from future takes.

### Which rule wins

For each generation Voyager merges the rules:

1. Rules whose `locale` does not match the production language are skipped and
   reported `locale_mismatch`.
2. Two rules for the same phrase (same locale and matching): the higher scope
   wins (production over project over workspace), reported as `shadowed` in
   `lexicon.conflicts`.
3. In the text, the longest match wins ("Voyager Studio" over "Voyager"); a shorter
   rule inside it is reported `overlapped`.

### After a rule changes

- Existing takes never change. A take whose text contains an affected phrase
  shows `lexiconChanged: true`; takes without the phrase are unaffected.
- Regenerate the affected passage (a repair) or the whole take, per the model's
  repair scope ([takes and repairs](#takes-approval-and-repairs)).
- Captions keep the display spelling.

## Edit a script in place from chat

When the user asks for a change to the open production ("make line 3 warmer"), edit the saved production, never regenerate from scratch. Read `voyager voice agent production` first, send its current `revision` as `expectedRevision` on every write, and on `revision_conflict` read again, re-apply only your change to the newer record and retry. The user sees what you changed in the Voice panel, marked "Updated by the agent".

| The user says                             | Call                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ----------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| "Make line 3 warmer", "more excited here" | `production_update` with a `direction` annotation on that line's words: `{kind: "direction", locator: {text: "…"}, instruction: "warmer"}` (add `tag` only where the model lists it)                                                                                                         |
| "Say Moda like MOH-duh"                   | `lexicon` `{action: "save", scope: "production", rule: {phrase: "Moda", respelling: "MOH-duh"}}` (project or workspace scope only when they ask); never change the script                                                                                                                    |
| "Give the last sentence to the guest"     | `production_update` with a `speaker` annotation: `{kind: "speaker", speakerId, locator: {text: "…"}}`. Take `speakerId` from `production.speakers`, never the name. No guest yet: add one with `speakers` (keep the existing entries with their `speakerId`), read the new id, then annotate |
| "Pause after the intro"                   | `production_update` with a `pause` annotation: `{kind: "pause", locator: {afterText: "…"}, pauseMs: 600}`                                                                                                                                                                                    |

A direction or pause list replaces the current direction and pause notes, so send the ones to keep along with the new one (read them from `production.annotations`). Speaker annotations add to `production.speakerRanges` instead and can be sent alone. Changing a recorded take is a new take or a `repair`; edits only change the next recording.

Use `voyager voice agent lexicon` rules, never respellings or markup in the script.

## Record whole takes; repair in scope

Before recording, read [managed narration preflight](#managed-narration-preflight).

For managed narration, request an advisory credit quote with the existing
`voyager voice agent capabilities --input '{"model":"MODEL_ID","text":"PROVIDER_TEXT"}' --json`.
Include direction tags and pronunciation expansions in the supplied text. Relay
`creditEstimate.label` (for example, "about 8 Voyager credits (dollar cost unknown)")
and use that quote as the cost in "Approve and record". The shared cost owner uses
the model's live provider price, including promotions, and its declared Unicode or
UTF-8 billing unit. Unknown model, rate or unit means unknown credits. Compilation can change the text and
usage, so this advisory quote is not a maximum or admission. No narration dollar
quote or bound is available. `voice agent` has no `estimate` operation, and
`generate`/`audition` have no `dryRun`.

Use the tool's credit-only label.

- `voyager voice agent generate` records the script as one take. When the shared spend decision permits it, record by default and show the script beside the take. Ask first when the user asked to approve scripts or is clearly reviewing step by step, with "Approve and record" and its cost as the first option and no option marked "(Recommended)", and "approve" in the question text ("Approve this script before recording?"): the question waits for them, and only their answer is permission to record. Never re-ask once they said to proceed, and a changed script gets one more look only when they are reviewing step by step.
- Build captions and the edit from the selected take. When the user chooses a take or delegates selection, call `take_select` before building; this is the product's approval operation, not evidence that the user listened. Present the video with `voyager files present` and `--voiceover TAKE_ID` for the take it plays, so the chat and Voice tab show it; Voyager checks the take is in its sound.
- A "Use Take N … re-time the cuts" message (sent from the Voice tab) names the take and video: approve that take, re-time the narration-driven cuts to its word timings (`voyager voice agent take`), render the next version and present it with `--voiceover` for that take; generate no new voice audio.

## Takes, approval and repairs

### Revisions and request keys

- Every write and every paid call carries `expectedRevision`, the production's
  `revision` from your last read.
- Every paid call carries a `requestKey` you choose (1–160 characters, such as
  your tool-call id). Repeating the call with the same key and the same
  parameters returns the same attempt, even if the script or voice changed
  meanwhile, and never starts a second paid job. Use it after a timeout or an
  unclear failure. A new take needs a new key.

### Generating a take

`voyager voice agent generate {productionId, expectedRevision, requestKey}` records the whole
script (or one speaker's parts with `speakerId`) as one take. It returns
`attemptId`, `jobId`, `characters` and `estimatedCredits` and runs in the
background.

- **Estimate and spend.** Before the paid call, read
  [managed narration preflight](#managed-narration-preflight)
  and the capability credit quote above.
- **Speakers.** A `range` that spans two speakers is refused unless every speaker is a Fish Audio voice on a multi-speaker model ([Fish Audio voices](references/casting.md#fish-audio-voices)); otherwise generate each speaker's part separately.

#### Waiting and job state

| Attempt `state` | Meaning                                                                                                                            |
| --------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `failed`        | Nothing to use; read `error.code` and `error.message`.                                                                             |
| `uncertain`     | The provider may have received the request; it was not charged. Voyager never resubmits it. Offer a new take (a new `requestKey`). |

`voyager voice agent generate`, `voyager voice agent repair` and `voyager voice agent convert` return a `jobId`. Voyager
does not resume the conversation when a voice job finishes, so wait with
`voyager jobs wait JOB_ID... --json` (repeat while pending) and never end the
turn on a pending take. Once the job is done, read `voyager voice agent take {attemptId}` for
the imported take.
Jobs survive an app restart and resume without another charge. To stop one,
`voyager jobs cancel JOB_ID`; a take that finished after the cancel was charged
and is kept (`completedAfterCancel`).

### Takes

`voyager voice agent production` lists takes; `voyager voice agent take {takeId}` gives one in detail.

| Field               | Use                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `kind`              | `full`, `passage` (a repair), `assembled` (a passage cut into its parent), `edited` (an exact pause), `converted`, `audition`, `preview`. Only full, assembled, edited and converted takes can be approved (`selectable`). |
| `selected`          | The approved take: the one to build captions and the edit with.                                                                                                                                                            |
| `direction`         | The preset and global tag it was made with; name it when two takes of one script differ.                                                                                                                                   |
| `audioAbsolutePath` | Where the audio is; use it in edits, question options and handoffs. Files live under `voice/<productionId>/` in the project.                                                                                               |
| `stale`             | Made from an older script revision.                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `lexiconChanged`    | A pronunciation rule affecting its words changed since.                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `alignment`         | `complete`, `partial`, `mismatch` or `none`. Word timings (`transcriptPath`) exist for complete and partial.                                                                                                               |
| `loudness`          | Integrated LUFS and true peak, measured on import.                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `assetStatus`       | `ok`, `missing`, `changed` or `unchecked`.                                                                                                                                                                                 |

Use the take's audio in edits from `audioAbsolutePath`. For captions and cuts,
use its transcript (`transcriptPath`, a speech transcript with word ids) with
the `edit-video` speech-edit tools, rather than transcribing again.

### Approving

- `voyager voice agent take_select {productionId, expectedRevision, takeId}` approves a take
  (the field keeps its wire name, `selectedTakeId`). A stale take needs
  `confirmStale: true`; say that its words are older than the script.
- `voyager voice agent take_select {productionId, expectedRevision, undo: true}` restores the
  previous approval.

### Repairs

A repair re-records part of a take ("more energy on the reveal", a misread
word) and leaves the original intact.

1. **Plan it free.** `voyager voice agent repair {kind: "passage", takeId, range,
instruction?, dryRun: true}` returns `repairPlan`: `scope` (`passage` or
   `whole_take`), `boundaryText` (the words that will be re-recorded) and a
   plain `reason`, with `estimatedCredits`. Nothing is charged.
2. **Run it** with the same parameters, `dryRun` off, and a new `requestKey`.
   The result is a `passage` take.
3. **Assemble** once the passage is accepted: `voyager voice agent repair {kind: "assemble",
takeId: <parent>, passageTakeId}` cuts at the silences around the passage
   (local, no charge) and creates an `assembled` take.

- `scope: "whole_take"` forces a full re-record; use it when a change affects
  the whole read (a new voice, preset or tone).
- The parent must match the current script: after a script edit, record a new full take instead.
- Assembly needs word timings covering the replaced words; offer a whole take instead.

A repair uses the production's direction plus the `instruction` (`preset`,
`tag`, `settings`).

### Exact pauses

`voyager voice agent repair {kind: "pause", takeId, at: {afterText: "Voyager."}, durationMs:
800}` makes the silence between two aligned words exactly 800 ms (50–10000).
It is a local audio edit with no Voyager call and no charge; the result is an
`edited` take with updated word timings and captions. It needs a take with word
timings, and `at` must fall between two words. The edited take needs its own
approval.

### Standalone command line

Outside a conversation, the `voyager voice` commands do the paid
work without a production record: `voyager voice capabilities`, `voice search`,
`voice audition`, `voice generate` and `voice convert` create
ordinary media jobs (collect with `voyager jobs wait` and `jobs result`). Pass
the same `--request-id` to retry.

## Convert a performance

"Read it like me": `voyager voice agent convert` re-voices the user's recorded read in the cast voice (their timing, not their identity). On the user's own ElevenLabs key, `voyager speech convert` does the same with a premade or their own ElevenLabs voice. See [performance](references/performance.md).

## Check and hand off

Report production and take state from `voyager voice agent take`/`voyager voice agent production`. Describe the inspection actually performed (listening, transcription or measurement).

Transcribe each finished take and diff it against the script to catch omitted or misread words; provider alignment is not an independent check. Use `voyager speech transcribe TAKE --local --output DIR` and [check-take.py](scripts/check-take.py). Keep the take's own word timings for captions and cuts.
